news.headline: Scientists Use Drones and Whale Snot to Learn About Whales
news.body: Scientists flew small drones with clean petri dishes through the misty breath of a whale to collect samples. From that whale snot they read the animal's whole set of genes, a first! It's a safer way to check on whales than older methods that needed darts.

news.headline: Spacecraft Arrives at Mercury After an Eight-Year Trip
news.body: The BepiColombo mission, built by Europe and Japan, reached Mercury after traveling for eight years. It will adjust its path over the next few months and start studying the planet in April. Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, and scientists hope to learn how it formed.
